items.text: Civil servants are fiercely dedicated to serving our community and this country. They do not deserve the treatment that the Trump Administration has offered, and their stories cannot be dismissed. https://t.co/igp9iOVzYf

Medicaid provides more than one in five Americans with health coverage. Last week, I joined my colleagues in filing an amicus brief in support of Medicaid patients’ right to exercise agency and autonomy when choosing their provider. https://t.co/LYet08uxtU

Today marks the 15th anniversary of the Affordable Care Act being signed into law. The ACA was a monumental piece of legislation that provided so many more Marylanders with health insurance and increased access to quality care. I will always work to protect and expand coverage for #MD03—including fighting cuts to Medicaid.

1 in 8 U.S. women are at risk of an invasive breast cancer diagnosis during their lifetime. Groups like the @NBCCStopBC and programs like the DOD’s Breast Cancer Research Program are leading the path forward for breast cancer research and advocacy, and I am committed to uplifting their work and championing this life-saving funding here in the halls of Congress. Special thanks to constituents, Angela from Elkridge and Robyn from Glen Burnie, for visiting!

The nonpartisan, independent Congressional Budget Office just confirmed what we’ve been saying for months: you can’t cut funding for Medicaid without millions of people losing their health coverage.

My heart is with President Biden, Dr. Biden, and his whole family following the President’s cancer diagnosis. Sending his family strength and praying for a swift and full recovery.

Nearly 20 hours into the Rules Committee hearing, I used my time to speak out on behalf of the millions of Americans who depend on Medicaid and food assistance. This so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” comes at the cost of programs that #MD03 and folks around the country depend on. That’s why I’ll be voting no.

Medicaid is a lifeline for so many in our community, including Jane and David from Ellicott City. Medicaid is not just a line item on a budget, it’s health care for our neighbors. https://t.co/NK4y3ThKyf

Not only will House Republicans’ Big Beautiful Bill result in deep Medicaid cuts, but it will trigger $500 billion in cuts to Medicare as well. That means, if enacted, this legislation will be the largest loss of health care coverage in American history. https://t.co/4YBhm878m6

Once again, Republicans are eyeing – not just cuts to Medicaid – but also Medicare. Make no mistake, if enacted, this would be the largest loss of health care coverage in American history.

The best parts of my district work weeks are being back in the MD03 community and talking about the issues that impact you most. At @HoCoHCCA's annual meeting, we talked about the importance of investing in our schools and healthcare system. As your representative on Capitol Hill, I can’t do my job without hearing from all of you. A special thank you to President Stu Kohn for your commitment and leadership on behalf of Howard County.

During this Save Our Hospitals Week of Action, I visited @umbwmc to see operations firsthand and have a frank discussion about potential funding cuts coming from Washington. UMBWMC and their first responder partners are doing some incredibly innovative things to reduce emergency department wait times, focus on long-term patient health, and save lives. Hospitals across Maryland and the nation already operate on razor-thin budgets, and the nearly $1 trillion cut to health care proposed in the President’s Big Beautiful Bill would put their life-saving programs and services at direct risk. It’s why I voted no last month – and will vote no again when the Senate sends the bill back to the House.

Yesterday, the Supreme Court ruled that states can cut off Medicaid funding to Planned Parenthood - even for care not related to abortion. This dangerous decision uses the pretext of abortion to defund and deny cancer screenings, prenatal services, and other forms of life-saving care. Patients should have more health care options, not less.

The attacks on fundamental rights and health care in the President’s so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” can’t be overstated. In addition to slashing Medicaid funding broadly, the Senate’s bill includes language to block Planned Parenthood from receiving Medicaid funding, which would be devastating to hundreds of clincis across the nation. After the attack on Planned Parenthood by the Supreme Court last week, it’s more crucial now than ever to stand up to abortion access and quality health care – I will be voting no.

House Democrats are united in voting against President Trump’s Big Ugly Bill. When it comes to gutting Medicaid, slashing SNAP, and cutting millions of jobs, we’re voting no. We just need four Republicans to join us. https://t.co/vC6gcBenZI

Last week, House Republicans voted to kick 17 million people off their health care – including seniors with diabetes, Americans with pre-existing conditions, and millions of children. These cuts to Medicaid also directly threaten the care that our nation’s rural hospitals provide. We will not stand by as Republicans strip away health care. The fight for quality, affordable care across the  country continues.

Nearly 33,000 military families rely on TRICARE to provide quality health care to their dependents. However, unlike private insurance, TRICARE only allows dependents to stay on their parents’ health insurance until they are 21. That’s why I’ve co-sponsored the bipartisan Health Care Fairness for Military Families Act to bridge this coverage gap so servicemembers and their dependents have the same access to health care as their civilian counterparts.

60 years ago today, President Johnson signed the Social Security Amendments of 1965, establishing Medicaid and Medicare. When these health care programs were first established, they had overwhelming bipartisan support to provide health care for our most vulnerable Americans — including millions of children and seniors. Now, through President Trump’s Big Ugly Law, Republicans are ripping away this critical health coverage.

Every day, @MDCancerCare gives patients hope through integrated, evidence-based cancer care and clinical research. Their physicians, doctors, and directors break down barriers to care and ease the stress of patients and families when navigating some of their hardest days. From expanding community opportunities to federal policy,  I will keep fighting to ensure our doctors have the resources they need to provide care, and that every Marylander has access to the high-quality care they deserve.

The Planned Parenthood of Maryland is a crucial part of many Marylanders’ health care, providing lifesaving cancer screenings, STI testing and treatment, and family planning resources to over 33,000 patients in Maryland alone. But the President’s Big Ugly Bill and a recent Supreme Court decision are now on the verge of blocking Medicaid funds for even Planned Parenthood’s non-abortion services. I had a chance to visit Annapolis’ Planned Parenthood facility to discuss how we can continue supporting their lifesaving care in Congress in the face of these cuts.

By far one of the most damaging outcomes of President Trump’s Big, Ugly Law was blocking Medicaid funding for Planned Parenthood. Planned Parenthood provides more than just reproductive resources; they provide lifesaving cancer screenings, STI testing, and are often some of the only health care Americans in medically underserved communities receive in a year. But now, nearly 200 facilities are at risk of closure. I’ve joined more than 130 of my colleagues across the House and Senate to introduce legislation to repeal these provisions that would threaten access to lifesaving resources for millions across the country.
